model_output.score_comment_short: Your projects show practical development, but the internship bullets leave key work unspecified.
model_output.score_comment_long: BuckeyeBites names a useful set of features and technologies. The Cardinal Health internship identifies the application and stack, but not the features you developed or problems you solved. Adding a concrete example from that work would make the fastest difference.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can see an entry-level software engineering direction and relevant hands-on work. The resume gives them less to assess about your individual technical choices.
model_output.first_impression: You have a computer science degree, a software engineering internship, and several projects. BuckeyeBites stands out because it names both user-facing features and the stack. The internship description is less specific about what you built.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions" doesn't identify a requirement or solution, so a reviewer can't see what you contributed.
model_output.summary: Your Cardinal Health internship places you on an internal inventory application using React and Spring Boot. Alongside the campus food-ordering capstone, it points toward entry-level software engineering work with both front-end and back-end exposure. The capstone's authentication and shopping cart are worth keeping because they make the application more tangible. A reviewer may still wonder what you personally developed at Cardinal Health, making the internship harder to assess than the projects.
strengths: The internship names an internal inventory application and its React and Spring Boot stack, giving the work a technical setting.
The finance tracker pairs Python and matplotlib with SQLite, showing a different application and storage approach from BuckeyeBites.
The help desk role connects student and faculty support with documented solutions, showing experience responding to users' technical issues.
gaps: The internship doesn't identify an inventory feature or bug, leaving the actual engineering work difficult to distinguish.
The unit-test bullet names an intended purpose but not what the tests covered, so the reader can't judge their technical focus.
The capstone lists authentication and a cart but doesn't explain how either was implemented, leaving your technical choices unclear.
